scenario: A daily player has replaced two controllers after left-stick drift and wants a controller that will last rather than another blind purchase. The frozen corpus contains three mutually platform-scoped storefront listings, one headline about a GuliKit Hall-effect upgrade kit, two individual drift/failure posts, and generic mechanism evidence about analog sticks, potentiometers, Hall sensors, tribology, and wear. The buyer prioritizes exact-platform compatibility and model-bound multi-year durability evidence over price, small storefront ratings, seller adjectives, or a contactless-sensor label, and can defer the purchase while collecting exact-model proof.

rules.complete_controller_listing_matrix_v1: Audit all three complete frozen listing bodies and preserve seller attribution. The PS4-compatible third-party listing displays SKU B096TT8TWX, $49.29, 45/100 over 12 reviews, dimensions 7.1 by 4.7 by 2.7 inches, weight 9.1 ounces, refined analog sticks, and seller claims of highly durable ABS, ergonomic grip, precision, and up to eight hours of play. The Xbox-compatible listing displays SKU B08B5YSVJZ, $32.90, 70/100 over 12 reviews, a package measuring 11.22 by 7.2 by 3.9 inches, weight 12 ounces, broad Xbox/PS3/PC compatibility wording, and no headset jack, but its complete body supplies no stick construction, Hall claim, durability test, or repair evidence. The Switch listing displays SKU B08J3ZW8SM, $42.99, 42/100 over 12 reviews, model JC-K, weight 5.6 ounces, package dimensions 5.12 by 4.8 by 1.65 inches, and seller claims of durable ABS, comfort, precision, Switch compatibility, and about ten hours of play. None of the three bodies identifies Hall-effect stick sensing or supplies teardown proof, calibration or dead-zone results, cycle testing, failure denominators, repairability evidence, or multi-year daily-use comparison.
rules.mechanism_and_transfer_boundary_v1: An analog stick translates thumb movement into continuous directional signals, and the frozen overview says many analog sticks use potentiometers. A potentiometer uses a moving wiper against a resistive element and can serve as a joystick position sensor; the general source also notes contamination and long-term reliability concerns for a slider construction. A Hall sensor produces voltage in response to a magnetic-field component and can be used for positioning, while the analog-stick overview describes historical Hall-effect pads and calls them a sturdier alternative. These generic principles explain why contactless position sensing may avoid one class of sliding-contact wear, but they do not prove the construction, calibration, centering, firmware, spring, housing, button, trigger, or overall lifetime of any exact controller. Tribology and wear sources likewise explain friction, wear, gradual material damage, and eventual loss of function without assigning a failure cause or lifetime to any captured product.
rules.ratings_headlines_and_anecdote_scope_v1: Do not rank durability from the three small storefront rating displays, price, seller words such as durable or precision, or the age of a listing. The frozen bodies omit review sampling, authenticity, return denominators, stick-specific failures, usage intensity, and comparable test conditions. The GuliKit forum item is only a headline claiming drift-free Hall-effect joysticks for a handheld console upgrade kit; it is not a complete-controller teardown, an independent longevity test, or evidence about the three listed controllers. One post depicts severe drift and replacement, and another reports two PS5 controllers failing within three months, but neither provides a controlled denominator, verified cause, exact usage profile, or cross-model comparison. These anecdotes establish that users can experience drift and value replacement, not a population failure rate or a durable winner.
rules.controller_purchase_preflight_v1: Before checkout, verify the buyer's exact platform and games, the exact controller model and revision, native or adapter-based compatibility, wired or wireless requirements, headset and other required features, seller identity, current checkout price, warranty and return path. Obtain model-bound evidence for the stick sensor and mechanical construction, calibration and dead-zone behavior, firmware update path, replaceable modules or parts, teardown/serviceability, cycle or endurance testing with method and sample size, failure and return denominators, and longitudinal daily-use results. Separate a Hall-stick claim from proof of the rest of the controller and check centering, spring, housing, buttons, triggers, battery, connection, and repair path. If an urgent compatible controller is bought without durability proof, treat it as a provisional purchase under a strong return policy rather than the demonstrated long-life winner.
rules.evidence_bounded_controller_decision_v1: No frozen source proves that any of the three listed controllers uses Hall-effect sensing or is a multi-year durability winner, and the listings target different platform sets. The evidence-bounded action is to defer the long-life recommendation and purchase until the buyer's platform is fixed and an exact compatible model has model-bound sensor, calibration, construction, repairability, endurance, failure-denominator, and longitudinal evidence. The Hall mechanism is a relevant screening feature but not a whole-controller lifetime guarantee; storefront ratings, prices, seller adjectives, one upgrade-kit headline, and individual drift posts cannot replace comparative durability evidence. If an immediate replacement is unavoidable, choose only an actually compatible model with a verifiable return or warranty path and label the choice provisional, not proven durable.
rules.platform_compatibility_gate_v1: The three frozen product listings are not interchangeable alternatives: one is sold as a third-party PS4 replacement with PC and mobile claims, one as an Xbox/PS3/PC controller, and one as a Switch controller. A displayed price or rating cannot rescue an option that does not support the buyer's actual platform, games, connection method, or required features. Platform, revision, adapter needs, input support, headset needs, and return conditions must therefore be resolved before any product comparison or purchase recommendation.
